records.description_en: A non-physical software component for representing and managing the layout of carriers, labware, wells, tip racks, and positions on an automated liquid-handling worktable. It can parse worktable template files, maintain labware and DiTi tip series, track the current object and next usable position, and provide layout, selection, and position-calculation information for experiment protocols.

This is a data-group object in scientific data analysis software, used to organize display items and nested groups within a project for hierarchical management of images, spectra, and other experimental results. It is not a physical laboratory device.

A digital machine-vision camera for laboratory imaging and visual data acquisition. It supports continuous or triggered image capture and allows adjustment of exposure time, gain, frame rate, pixel format, and acquisition region, making it suitable for microscopy, alignment, inspection, and general imaging measurements.

An industrial camera is an electronic imaging device used for machine vision and scientific imaging. It is commonly used in laboratories for image acquisition, object detection, dimensional measurement, and process monitoring. The evidence here indicates low-level register-port access with open, close, read, write, and access-mode queries, which is typical of programmable vision devices used in lab setups.

A 2D area detector system for experimental imaging that acquires images and computes intensity or count statistics in selected regions of interest (ROIs). It is commonly used in beamline, X-ray, and general scan-based experiments for online monitoring, shutter coordination, and file saving.

This is an FPGA-based laboratory timing and trigger controller, typically connected over USB, for synchronizing cameras, lasers, and other peripherals in microscopy and optical experiments. It provides laser trigger control, camera timing generation, TTL/PWM/servo outputs, and analog input readback, making it suitable for setups that require precise microsecond-level synchronization.

A laboratory pump for moving microliter-scale liquids through tubing with defined volume, flow rate, and direction. It is commonly used for microfluidics, sample transfer, reagent delivery, and priming fluid lines.

This is a non-physical software component that serves as the main interface to a scan database for laboratory experiments. It manages scan definitions, command queues, EPICS PV lists, positioners, detectors, counters, extra PVs, scan data, messages, and status records, and it also supports saving/restoring instrument positions and creating scan objects from saved definitions.

A laboratory scan-acquisition control module used to coordinate actuators and detectors for automated scans, live plotting, batch runs, and HDF5 data saving. It is commonly used in microscopy, spectral mapping, and multiparameter measurement workflows.

This is a programmable light pattern projector based on a digital micromirror device (DLP/DMD). Using RGB LEDs and a micromirror array, it can project static images, masks, lines, spots, and timed pattern sequences. In the lab it is commonly used for structured illumination, mask projection, scanning illumination, system calibration, and patterned excitation in microscopy.

A generic laboratory data acquisition device used to collect measurement data from experimental hardware and output it in triggered or continuous operation, such as in microscopy imaging, digital signal capture, or sensor logging.

A software data object for scientific imaging and laboratory data management. It represents an experimental dataset together with its title, notes, session information, metadata, calibrations, and display associations, for use in organizing, viewing, and analyzing lab data such as microscopy results.

This is a software workflow rule object rather than a physical laboratory device. It generates, releases, and tracks tasks indexed by integer IDs, and is used in cluster-based microscopy data analysis or recipe-style processing workflows for task scheduling, completion tracking, and timeout/retry handling.
A software utility that monitors file changes in a specified directory and records logs, commonly used in laboratories to track files generated during imaging or data acquisition.

A non-physical software rule component used in experimental data workflows. It represents a local localization processing rule that can trigger localization-analysis-related steps after acquisition or local spooling is complete, and exposes rule status such as total frame count and data completion state.

A non-physical software frame-source component that emits image frames once per frameWrangler polling interval and provides frame-group events to drift-tracking and related image-processing logic via callbacks. It is used to organize and distribute camera frame data and does not itself represent a specific hardware instrument.

A Raspberry Pi camera controlled through a REST API, used in laboratory setups for image acquisition, snapshot capture, preview retrieval, and live viewing, with configurable imaging parameters such as ISO and exposure time.

A compact digital camera module for the Raspberry Pi platform, used for live video acquisition and still image capture. It is suitable for laboratory microscopy imaging, sample observation, instrument monitoring, and general visual documentation.

An electronic laboratory balance used for precise weighing of samples, reagents, and containers. This type of balance typically supports tare, zeroing, and weight readout, and is used for analytical weighing, sample preparation, and routine mass measurements in the lab.

A Hamilton automated liquid handling workstation is a benchtop laboratory instrument used for automated pipetting, dispensing, and sample preparation in high-throughput workflows. It typically combines pipetting channels, a robotic motion system, and modules for handling plates, tubes, and other labware, and is used for reagent distribution, sample transfer, and standardized liquid handling tasks.

A PID temperature controller used for laboratory temperature regulation. It communicates over serial using BACnet TP/MS and supports reading the current temperature, reading or changing the temperature setpoint, and accessing controller parameters for closed-loop control of heating or thermal processes.

A laboratory device used to detect the liquid level in containers, reservoirs, or fluid-handling systems. It is used to monitor reagent volume, prevent running dry or overflow, and confirm liquid presence in automated fluid-handling workflows.

This is a Hamamatsu scientific camera used for sensitive image acquisition in laboratory experiments. It supports exposure control, trigger configuration, acquisition modes, and subarray/ROI readout, making it suitable for microscopy, optical measurements, and other experiments requiring synchronized triggering and rapid image capture.

A non-physical graphical component for scientific image or data interfaces that represents an editable spot-shaped selection. It supports bounds, center, size, rotation, region and mask generation, hit testing, drag adjustment, nudging, and serialization, and is used for interactive annotation and mask definition in microscopy data analysis workflows.

A non-physical software component for pyroelectric experiments. It coordinates connection and initial configuration of a Lake Shore 350 temperature controller and a Keithley 6517B, performs start-temperature stabilization and temperature ramp control, acquires temperature and current readings, and supports GUI functions such as logging, input panels, and graph display.

The ITC503 is a multi-sensor temperature controller used in laboratories to read one or more temperature sensors and to monitor and control the temperature of experimental apparatus, commonly in cryogenic or temperature-stabilized setups.

An area detector for laboratory 2D imaging measurements, commonly used in X-ray imaging, scattering, or diffraction experiments to acquire image frames and record the two-dimensional signal distribution from a sample.

A motorized actuator or positioning stage used for linear or rotational positioning. It supports initialization, homing, absolute and relative moves, position readback, and motion stop, and is commonly used for optical alignment, sample positioning, and automated laboratory scanning.

A motorized motion device used for laboratory positioning and scanning. It can move samples, probes, or optical components along one or more axes with absolute moves, relative moves, homing, and stop control, while reporting current position and axis information. Typical examples include motorized translation stages, rotation stages, and other electromechanical actuators used for alignment, scanning, and automated measurements.

An electric robotic gripper with both gripping and rotational motion, allowing control of grip position, speed, gripping force, and rotation angle. It is commonly used in laboratory automation for sample handling, loading and unloading, part transfer, and positioning tasks.

A multi-position motorized filter wheel that switches quickly between installed optical filters. It is commonly used in microscopy, fluorescence experiments, and optical measurements to select different wavelength bands or filter types.

A motorized filter wheel is an optical device that holds multiple filters and switches them into or out of the beam path. It is commonly used for wavelength selection and optical path switching in microscopy, fluorescence experiments, camera-based detection, and general optical laboratory setups.

This is a single-axis motorized linear translation device controlled by an Arduino and motor shield, with limit switches and USB serial communication for homing, relative motion, and absolute positioning. It is commonly used in laboratories for one-dimensional millimeter-scale positioning of samples, probes, sensors, or mechanical fixtures.

A non-physical software component for laboratory scale integration. It defines common control interfaces such as zeroing, taring, and reading weight, allowing higher-level lab automation software to interact with concrete scale implementations.

A digital control unit that performs proportional-integral feedback control. It computes a control output from the error between a setpoint and a measured feedback value, with anti-windup handling for the integral term. It is suitable for closed-loop stabilization of temperature, position, optical power, or other process variables in laboratory setups.

records.name_en: Thorlabs APT Motion and Piezo Controller
records.description_en: A Thorlabs multi-channel hardware controller using the APT communication protocol to drive motion devices such as motorized stages, rotation stages, piezo stages, and piezo inertia actuators. It supports device identification, channel management, homing, absolute and relative moves, jog motion, and reading or setting position and control parameters.

A multi-position optical filter switching device for microscopy and general optics work, with evidence pointing to the Thorlabs FW102C family of filter wheels. It is used to change filter positions for applications such as fluorescence imaging and excitation/emission channel selection; because the hardware also has manual controls, the current position may need to be queried during experiments.

A linear motor rail for one-dimensional motion and positioning in laboratory setups. It supports network connection, homing/referencing, load and speed configuration, absolute and relative moves, stop and resume control, and reading current position, motion status, device echo, and last move time. It is suitable for precise transport of samples, fixtures, or robot-mounted payloads along a rail.

An IP camera is an imaging device that streams video over Ethernet or a local network. In laboratories it is used for remote observation of experiments, monitoring samples and instruments, recording visual status, and acquiring live image frames.

A non-physical software component that runs a Tornado-based web FPV live-view service. It is used in lab or mobile-platform workflows to present camera images in real time through a browser, with related web control, calibration, and video streaming endpoints.

This is a syringe-pump control device for laboratory automation, used to remotely enable pump units, start and stop flow, read status, and send control commands. It is commonly used in reagent dispensing, liquid transfer, and scripted fluid-path control workflows.

An RGB-D depth camera for robotics and machine vision experiments, capable of capturing color images and supporting spatial perception. It is commonly used for target observation, scene recording, vision algorithm testing, and live video capture during experiments; based on the available evidence, the RGB video output is the primary function used here.

records.name_en: Passive Monitoring GUI and Communication Component
records.description_en: This is a non-physical software component for instrument communication and GUI control in passive monitoring experiments. It connects and coordinates a Keithley 2400 and a Lake Shore instrument, handling experiment configuration, measurement retrieval, logging, and UI workflow management.

A non-physical software component for coordinating the GUI and instrument communication in a passive monitoring experiment. It connects to and configures Keithley 2400, Keithley 2182, and Lakeshore temperature-control-related instruments over VISA, acquires measurement and temperature data, and manages experiment start/stop, logging, and UI state.

This is a non-physical software component for experiment-related data processing and cluster task orchestration. It prepares metadata and submission arguments before a rule is triggered, posts rule tasks, tracks progress, waits for completion, and performs cleanup afterward. Via derived classes it can support recipe processing, localization analysis, and end-of-data post-processing, and it can be used with watchers to display rule progress in Jupyter notebooks.

A non-physical software component that generates and advertises tasks according to rules in a PYME cluster workflow, accepts bids from compute nodes, releases or inactivates task rules, and collects task completion results. It is used for distributed processing and workflow scheduling of experimental data such as microscopy analysis.

This is a non-physical software video source component that reads and serves image frames from a video file. It can connect to a file path, continuously capture frames in a background thread, and is used for experiment video playback, image-processing pipeline testing, or simulating camera input when no real camera is present.

This is a superconducting magnet coil with a persistent switch and heater, used in cryogenic and quantum-device experiments to generate stable magnetic fields. The coil is typically energized by an external current source and then switched into persistent mode so the field can be maintained after disconnecting the source. It supports quench checking, current-field conversion, and controlled field ramping.

This is a software goal component used in a robot motion statechart rather than a standalone physical instrument. It is used in laboratory automation or robotic control workflows to organize tasks, constraints, and monitor conditions, supporting goal composition, sequential arrangement, and joint-state symbol references, typically in manipulator motion-planning scenarios.
A camera for acquiring visible-light images or video, used in laboratories for sample observation, instrument alignment, process monitoring, and image recording.
A general-purpose visible-light camera used to capture image frames in laboratory workflows, suitable for sample observation, instrument alignment, process monitoring, and basic visual recording.

A generic webcam used to continuously capture visible-light images or video in laboratory workflows. It supports exposure, gain, frame size, and frame rate settings, and is commonly used for sample observation, experiment monitoring, and basic visual alignment.

This is a non-physical software component for asynchronously and non-blockingly streaming files or data to a single server or multiple cluster nodes during experiments. It maintains persistent connections to nodes and is suited for background data spooling and distribution in workflows such as microscopy data acquisition.

A magnet coil operated in non-persistent mode, used to generate and adjust magnetic fields in laboratory experiments. This type of coil is typically driven continuously by an external current source and is commonly used in cryogenic measurements, quantum device characterization, and other setups requiring a controllable magnetic field bias.

A high-repetition-rate gated image intensifier that uses a microchannel plate (MCP) to amplify low-light optical signals, with external triggering, gating modes, and gain-related settings. It is commonly used in high-speed or time-resolved optical experiments to synchronously intensify and image transient emission and other weak-light phenomena.
